paper.title: Dielectric tensor prediction for inorganic materials using latent information from preferred potential
paper.research_summary: This study leverages multi-rank equivariant structural embeddings from a universal neural network potential to enhance predictions of dielectric tensors. We develop an equivariant readout decoder to predict total, electronic, and ionic dielectric tensors while preserving O(3) equivariance, and benchmark its performance against state-of-the-art algorithms. Virtual screening of thermodynamically stable materials from Materials Project for two discovery tasks, high-dielectric and highly anisotropic materials, identifies promising candidates including Cs2Ti(WO4)3 (band gap Eg = 2.93eV, dielectric constant ε = 180.90) and CsZrCuSe3 (anisotropic ratio αr = 121.89). The results demonstrate our model’s accuracy in predicting dielectric tensors and its potential for discovering novel dielectric materials.

task.task_name_raw: Dielectric tensor prediction for inorganic materials
task.objective: Predict the three types of dielectric tensors, ε∞ij, ε0ij and εij, for inorganic materials across 72 supported elements with the equivariance to the input structure.
constraints: thermodynamic stability (Ehull = 0) for virtual screening candidates
input_requirements: 72-element support (excluding noble gases He, Ne, Ar, Kr)

evidence.text: In this study, we propose Dielectric Tensor Neural Network(DTNet) to predict the three types of dielectric tensors, ε1 ij , ε0 ij and εij, for inorganic materials across 72 supported elements with the equivairance to the input structure.

The challenge of GNN in materials science is that they usually require a large number of data to prevent models from overfitting, while such chemical data are generally expensive to collect either from simulation or experiments.

stages.stage_goal: Obtain DFT-calculated dielectric tensor data for training and evaluation.
stage_output: 7277 relaxed materials with calculated dielectric constants

evidence.text: We leverage on one of the largest open databases of DFT-calculated crystal structure properties, Materials Project38, to obtain a wide range of training structures. The dataset (MP v2023.11.1) contains 7277 relaxed materials along with calculated dielectric constants.

stages.stage_goal: Clean the raw MP dataset by restricting dielectric constant ranges and filtering out unsupported elements.

evidence.text: We clean up the dataset by restricting the element in total dielectric constants εij ∈[−10, 100] for ∀i, j∈{1,2,3} and filtering out structures that contain elements not supported by PFP. Finally there are 6648 structures retained for model training.

stages.stage_name_raw: Training DTNet with pretrained PFP encoder
stages.stage_goal: Train the equivariant readout decoder using frozen PFP-L4 features as input.
stage_output: trained DTNet models for ε∞, ε0, and ε prediction

evidence.text: By leveraging a pretrained PFP model as an efﬁcient and expressive encoder, we demonstrated that the pretrained PFP processes a rich set of high-order latent compositional and structural information for tensorial property prediction.
PFP-L4 is taken as the feature generator and is utilized for the subsequent study.

stages.stage_goal: Evaluate DTNet performance using MAEten, MAEmean-diag, MAEdiag, and MAEoff-diag metrics on test set and Matbench.
stage_output: MAEten = 0.368 for ε∞, 1.677 for ε0, 1.911 for ε

evidence.text: To evaluate the performance of DTNet, we compared it against existing methods, PaiNN31, M3GNet36 and MatTen37, on the dataset obtained from Materials Project (MP)38.

stages.stage_name_raw: Preparation of candidate structures for virtual screening
stages.stage_goal: Download and filter thermodynamically stable non-metal materials from MP for screening.

evidence.text: To prepare the candidate set for screening, we downloaded 14,375 non-metal materials from the MP database. These materials are speciﬁcally selected based on the energy above convex hull Ehull = 0 to estimate their thermodynamic stability, so that only stable materials are included in the candidate set.

stages.stage_name_raw: Iterative active learning for virtual screening
stages.stage_goal: Identify top candidates for high-dielectric and highly anisotropic materials using ensemble DTNet predictions and UCB acquisition function.
stage_output: 60 top candidates (20 per round × 3 rounds) for each discovery task

evidence.text: We conducted iterative active learning to identify top candidates through virtual screening.

stages.stage_goal: Validate top candidates using density functional perturbation theory calculations.
stage_output: 35 converged DFPT results for high-dielectric task
41 converged DFPT results for anisotropic task

evidence.text: To validate the promising materials identiﬁed by DTNet, we conducted a three-round active exploration, with each round proposing 20 top candidates for validation.
Finally, totally 35 out of the 60 structures across 3 iterations are successfully converged through ﬁrst-principle calculations.
Consequently, 41 out of the 60 screened structures were successfully validated via DFPT computations.
